title: Crowds queuing for her records; a book reports her dead
summary: Reitz says fans queued at Clarence Williams's store for her records; Wallace knew nothing of it and found a book listing her as dead in 1952.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: You know, I heard and read that when a record of yours would come out in Chicago, people would stand in line at Clarence William's Store. That's what I heard, stand in long lines, a block long, to get a new record by Sippie Wallace.

I know. I know in Dallas, Texas some people would stand in line. I was (unintelligible) tell me that for three or two weeks, that people would stay out there two weeks (unintelligible). A line as long as you could see.
How did that make you feel as a young girl?
I didn't know everybody was out there. I didn't know they was out there.
Did you know about it in Chicago?
That they stood in line at Clarence William's Store?

No, I never know. I heard (unintelligible) at Louisiana-Alley last year, they had (unintelligible) my daughter, she go to college, and she bought one of those books and she pulled a leaf out, they say I was dead. Said I died in '52.

Said I was dead. (Unintelligible). I said, no, I wouldn't do that, maybe she got the wrong understanding, you know. It might be (unintelligible). So when I went to (unintelligible). But why they have me, say I died in '52. (Unintelligible).
Well, you sure look alive to me. And you certainly very lively.
